findings.reason: two nodes and their gates would be spent rebuilding changes that are already on main, and the plan's declared state would keep lying about them.
findings.text: §2 declares status `implementable` while its own deliverable text says "Built as `e7bfe1da15`", and §4 does the same at line 51 for `dc1f1b01ac`; both changes are present in the tree (`reckon/crew/placement.py:102` `LOCAL_LANE_RESERVE`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:211,318` passing `reserve`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:776` with `"held"` already in `_PRE_LAUNCH_PHASES`), so a node dispatched on either section rebuilds landed work

findings.reason: a node can deliver those two cases green with no change at all and call the section done, so the gate proves nothing about the change it was dispatched for.
findings.text: §5, §6 and §7 (lines 57, 63, 69) declare only "the tests … add no failure against the base", a no-regression arm that passes on unfixed code, where §2 and §3 in the same plan state "It fails at base"; and §5's second case and §6's "review of a delivered run goes first" are already the base behaviour in `reckon/crew/queue_order.py:255-276` (`_next_to_launch` returns `reviews[0]` first, then the overridden row before the ranked one)

findings.reason: a node handed these done-whens must either stall waiting on another session's lane or record a measurement it never took, and the section cannot be closed on one verdict.
findings.text: §2's done-when closes on "nova's codex review … is dispatched once and launches", which needs another session to act and a metered lane to be serving; §6 (line 63) and §7 (line 69) close on "a measurement over one evening of live passes" and "a 120 s `py-spy record` of the live admit service … and the median launch duration over one evening falls below 15 s", none of which a single node can produce inside one node's turn, and §7 states an absolute bar with no base figure to measure a delta against

findings.reason: the second deliverable cannot be scoped, reviewed or closed on the same verdict as the first, and a node that lands the budget cannot be judged done while an unnamed repair is still open.
findings.text: §7 delivers two things: a pass bounded by a 60 s flight budget with per-launch duration recorded on the verdict row, and, as a separate deliverable, "repair the next largest per-launch cost the profile names", whose target is not known until the profile runs; its write paths are named as "the step the profile names" (the same at line 69)

findings.reason: without a named path each node puts its evidence wherever its worktree allows, so the arm that proves the section lands where no later reader can open it.
findings.text: none of §2 to §7 names where its all_debug arm, its `py-spy` profile or its evening measurement is written, while §8 does name `docs/evidence/fragments/the-escape-lane-and-reviews-keep-pace/queue-depth.html` (line 75) and sibling plans in the same sprint write each gate log under `docs/evidence/fragments/<slug>/s<N>.html` (93 of the repository's 237 plans name such a path)

findings.reason: a named function or write path is a guess the node must reconcile against the code, and a wrong guess costs a dispatch and a review round that the brief, not the plan, is where this belongs.
findings.text: the plan prescribes implementation rather than the endpoint: §2 names `reckon/crew/placement.py`, `dispatch_admission.py`, `_refuse_over_reservation_*` and `_local_lane_reserve` and says the two refusal functions "take a `reserve`" (the same shape at §4 line 51), and §5, §6 and §7 each carry an explicit "Write paths:" list (lines 57, 63, 69)

findings.reason: the mechanism the section argues is unchanged; only the count line needs correcting, and the reserve and its rationale stand on the six refusals it does enumerate.
findings.text: §1 says the review was "refused seven times … four times at the placement roster's cap … and twice at the reservation's cores bound"; the two classes account for six refusals, so the stated tally does not close over the total the same sentence asserts
